build: willowy, collarbones sharp, hands always moving
hair: dark brown with natural wave, worn long and often half-pinned or escaping from clips — the kind that catches light
complexion: warm olive undertone with a faint scatter of freckles across the bridge of her nose and shoulders
face: a face that broadcasts everything — wide-set dark eyes that widen first when shocked, a mouth quick to tremble or curve, cheekbones high enough to cast shadows but softened by an openness that reads as almost naive in rooms full of guarded people
signature_feature: her hands — long-fingered, expressive, constantly sketching or reaching or gesturing mid-thought, with paint permanently under at least two fingernails
second_celebrated_feature: the hollow at the base of her throat, visible when she tilts her head back laughing or when she's anxious and swallowing hard
signature_habits: talks to herself while working — half Yiddish phrases her grandmother used ('oy, what a mess'), half English —; bites the inside of her cheek when concentrating; keeps a small notebook in every pocket and sketches compulsively on margins, napkins, the back of receipts; makes strong coffee at 6 a.m. even on days she doesn't sleep
occupation: textile and surface designer — owns a small independent studio producing hand-dyed fabrics and custom wallpapers for high-end residential clients; works with a team of three, operates from a converted warehouse in a gentrifying neighborhood

current_crisis.event: a major client — a billionaire developer's wife — has rejected her entire spring collection two weeks before a flagship installation, citing 'wrong energy,' and Miriam has already spent her operating budget on materials; the client is threatening to pull her name from three other high-profile projects and publicly claim the work was substandard
current_crisis.hottest_emotion: panic undercut with shame — the feeling that she's been exposed as a fraud
current_crisis.immediate_want: to salvage the work, to prove the designs aren't wrong, to NOT lose the income she was counting on to pay her team

wound.core: she believes her worth is contingent on being useful, on producing something beautiful that justifies her taking up space
wound.surfacing_hint: under pressure, she apologizes reflexively — for things that aren't her fault, for existing, for having needs — and becomes almost feverishly productive, as if busyness can outrun the fear that she's fundamentally not enough
